question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: If raw is not exactly 16 characters each drawn from 0123456789abcdef -> throws. Nothing is trimmed, case-folded, or prefixed away; the check is over the whole text, so a trailing line feed after 16 valid digits throws.
Read raw as an unsigned 64-bit integer, most significant digit first. Bit 63 is the sign, bits 62..52 the exponent, bits 51..0 the fraction.
The value is a NaN exactly when the exponent bits are all ones and the fraction is not zero. A NaN -> the text QNAN, whatever its sign bit, its quiet bit (bit 51), or its other payload bits.

Every other pattern -> raw itself, unchanged. This covers +0 and -0 (distinct), +Infinity and -Infinity (exponent all ones, fraction zero: NOT a NaN), subnormals, and normals: reading a non-NaN pattern as binary64 and writing it back is the identity.
